He played college basketball for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]], and had a short, 19-game stint in the [[NBA]] with the [[Washington Wizards]]. ==High school career== Born in [[Baltimore, Maryland]],{{cite news|url=http://www.vuhoops.com/2012/11/26/3688296/2012-villanova-basketball-preview-daniel-ochefu|title=2012 Villanova Basketball Preview: Daniel Ochefu|first=Ed|last=Donohue|work=VU Hoops|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=26 November 2012|accessdate=5 April 2016}} Ochefu attended the [[Westtown School]], where he averaged 16 points and 12 rebounds per game as a junior. As a senior, he transferred to [[Downingtown East High School]]. He was ranked 54th on ESNPU's list of the top 100 players in his high school class.[http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/daniel_ochefu_812211.html "Daniel Ochefu"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180605212806/http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/daniel_ochefu_812211.html |date=2018-06-05 }}. villanova.com. Retrieved April 5, 2016. ==College career== Ochefu played college basketball for Villanova. As a freshman, he played behind center [[Mouphtaou Yarou]].{{cite news|last1=Juilano|first1=Joe|title=Villanova's Daniel Ochefu has emerged as a leader|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/20160401_Villanova_s_Daniel_Ochefu_has_emerged_as_a_leader.html|accessdate=September 25, 2016|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 31, 2016}} In 2013–14, he averaged 5.7 points per game as a reserve player. The following season, he had 9.2 points per game. Ochefu scored a career-high 25 points in a 73–63 win over St. John's on February 13, 2016. At the conclusion of the regular season, he was named Honorable Mention All-Big East.{{cite news|title=Four Named Unanimously to MBB All-BIG EAST First Team|url=http://www.bigeast.com/news/2016/3/6/MBB_0306160917.aspx|accessdate=March 9, 2015|work=[[Big East Conference]]|date=March 6, 2015}} Ochefu played in the NCAA championship game on April 4, 2016, against [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], where he helped the Wildcats defeat the Tar Heels 77–74, and claim Villanova's second national championship. ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2016–2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Ochefu joined the [[Washington Wizards]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]], where he averaged 1.8 points and 2.8 rebounds per game.{{cite news|title=Wizards' Daniel Ochefu: Struggles in summer league tryout|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-daniel-ochefu-struggles-in-summer-league-tryout/|accessdate=September 25, 2016|work=[[CBS Sports]]}} On September 23, 2016, he signed with the Wizards.{{cite web|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/09/23/wizards-finalize-training-camp-roster|title=Wizards Finalize Training Camp Roster|work=Wizards Today|date=September 23, 2016|accessdate=September 24, 2016|archive-date=March 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330221751/https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/09/23/wizards-finalize-training-camp-roster|url-status=dead}} He made his debut for the Wizards in their season opener on October 27, recording one rebound in four minutes off the bench in a 114–99 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://watch.nba.com/game/20161027/WASATL|title=Wizards at Hawks|work=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2016|accessdate=October 27, 2016}} ===Maine Red Claws (2017)=== On October 9, 2017, Ochefu was waived by the Wizards.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-waive-ochefu/|title=Wizards Waive Ochefu|work=Nba.com|date=October 9, 2017|accessdate=October 9, 2017}} The [[Boston Celtics]] signed him on October 13, 2017. He was assigned to G-League affiliate team the [[Maine Red Claws]]. === Windy City Bulls (2017–2018) === On November 30, 2017, Ochefu was acquired by the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{Cite web|title=Sports Digest: Red Claws trade Ochefu to Windy City|url=https://www.pressherald.com/2017/11/30/sports-digest-red-claws-trade-ochefu-to-windy-city/|access-date=January 30, 2022|website=Portland Press Herald|date=December 2017 }} ===Reno Bighorns / Stockton Kings (2018–2019)=== On February 12, 2018, Ochefu was traded by the Bulls to the [[Stockton Kings|Reno Bighorns]] along with a 2018 third-round draft pick and the returning player rights to [[Spencer Dinwiddie]] in exchange for Will Davis, the returning player rights to [[Lamar Patterson]], and a 2018 first-round draft pick.{{cite web|work=NBA.com|date=February 12, 2018|accessdate=February 12, 2018|url=http://reno.gleague.nba.com/news/bighorns-acquire-daniel-ochefu-2018-third-round-draft-selection-rights-spencer-dinwiddie-three-team-trade/|title=BIGHORNS ACQUIRE DANIEL OCHEFU, 2018 THIRD-ROUND DRAFT SELECTION AND RIGHTS TO SPENCER DINWIDDIE IN THREE-TEAM TRADE}} He remained on the team as it became the Stockton Kings.{{cite web |title=STOCKTON KINGS WAIVE FOUR PLAYERS |url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-waive-four-players/ |website=NBA.com |accessdate=November 3, 2018 |date=October 31, 2018 |archive-date=August 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809222623/https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-waive-four-players/ |url-status=dead }} Ochefu averaged 14 points and 8 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=Ibaraki Robots sign Daniel Ochefu, Nik Caner-Medley, Will Creekmore |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/ibaraki-robots-sign-daniel-ochefu-nik-caner-medley-will-creekmore/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=September 5, 2020 |date=August 5, 2019 |archive-date=August 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190806120029/https://sportando.basketball/en/ibaraki-robots-sign-daniel-ochefu-nik-caner-medley-will-creekmore/ |url-status=dead }} ===Overseas (2019–present)=== On April 2, 2019, [[CB Breogán|Cafés Candelas Breogán]] of the [[Liga ACB]] announced the signing of Ochefu.{{cite web|title=Daniel Ochefu, poderío interior para o Cafés Candelas Breogán|language=ES|url=http://www.cbbreogan.com/daniel-ochefu-poderio-interior-para-o-cafes-candelas-breogan|date=April 2, 2019|website=cbbreogan.com|accessdate=April 2, 2019}} In July 2019, Ochefu signed with the [[Ibaraki Robots]] in Japan.{{cite news |last1=Jensen |first1=Mike |title=Former Villanova Wildcat Daniel Ochefu signs to play in Japan |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/daniel-ochefu-nba-villanova-basketball-japan-g-league-contracts-20190731.html |accessdate=January 25, 2020 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=July 31, 2019}} In August 2022, he signed with the [[Rain or Shine Elasto Painters]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) as the team's import for the [[2022–23 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://mb.com.ph/2022/08/17/rain-or-shine-to-tap-daniel-ochefu-as-comms-cup-reinforcement/|title=Rain or Shine to tap Daniel Ochefu as Comm's Cup reinforcement|work=Manila Bulletin|date=August 17, 2022|accessdate=August 17, 2022}} However, he was replaced by [[Steve Taylor (basketball)|Steve Taylor]] prior to the start of the tournament.{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/rain-or-shine-changes-plans-steve-taylor-in-ochefu-out-a793-20220914|title=Change of plans for Rain or Shine as Taylor tapped to replace Ochefu|work=spin.ph|date=September 14, 2022|accessdate=September 14, 2022}} In February 2023, Ochefu signed with the [[TNT Tropang Giga]] as the team's import for the [[2023 EASL Champions Week]] held in Japan.{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/prince-ibeh-out-daniel-ochefu-in-as-other-tnt-import-in-easl-a793-20230216|title=Prince Ibeh out, Daniel Ochefu in as second TNT import in EASL|work=spin.ph|date=February 16, 2023|accessdate=February 20, 2023}} On September 20, 2023, Ochefu signed with the [[Hsinchu Lioneers]] of the [[P. League+]].{{cite web |title=Lioneers sign Daniel Ochefu |url=https://www.afrobasket.com/Nigeria/news/828857/Lioneers-sign-Daniel-Ochefu |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=9 November 2024 |date=20 September 2023}} On December 1, Ochefu left the team.{{cite web |title=首戰表現荒腔走板！攻城獅宣布3Q歐獅傅 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2634565 |publisher=ETtoday |access-date=9 November 2024 |date=1 December 2023}} In April 2024, Ochefu joined the [[Al-Jaish SC Syria (men's basketball)|Al-Jaish]] of the [[Syrian Basketball League]].{{cite web |title=Al Jaish adds Ochefu to their roster |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/867090/Al-Jaish-adds-Ochefu-to-their-roster |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=9 November 2024 |date=22 April 2024}} In first game of the quarterfinals, Ochefu scored 15 points, 12 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 block.{{cite web |title=Al Jalaa defeat Al Jaish in Game 1 |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Syria/news/867631/Al-Jalaa-defeat-Al-Jaish-in-Game-1 |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=9 November 2024 |date=25 April 2024}} On February 15, 2026, it was announced that Ochefu has signed with the [[Blackwater Bossing]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA).{{cite web |url=https://www.pba.ph/news/giants-are-coming-in-the-commissioner-s-cup |title=Giants are coming in the Commissioner's Cup |website=PBA.ph |date=February 15, 2026 |access-date=February 15, 2026 }} On March 21, 2026, he was replaced by [[Robert Upshaw]].{{cite web |first=Gerry |last=Ramos |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/blackwater-signs-import-robert-upshaw-to-replace-daniel-ochefu-a793-20260321 |title=Blackwater brings in seven-footer Robert Upshaw to replace Ochefu |website=Spin.ph |date=March 21, 2026 |access-date=March 21, 2026 }} ==International career== He was called up for the [[Nigeria national basketball team]] for the [[2017 FIBA Africa Championship]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.brila.net/diogu-ochefu-headline-nigerias-afrobasket-2017-final-roster/|title = Diogu, Ochefu headline Nigeria's AfroBasket 2017 final roster|date = 7 September
